title: No independent, cost-normalized comparison of open harnesses on the same open model
description: The only same-model harness comparisons found (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash across Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode/Pi/mini-SWE; Nemotron 3 Super across OpenHands/OpenCode/Codex) are run by the model authors and report no cost or token usage. The DeepSWE leaderboard reports cost per task but fixes the harness to mini-swe-agent, so harness-vs-harness cost/quality trade-offs on open models are unmeasured.

title: Harness choice moves open-model scores by up to ~9 points, but the variance is unreplicated
description: On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DeepSWE v1.1 ranges from 65.5 (OpenCode) to 74.2 (mini-SWE) depending on scaffold; on Nemotron 3 Super, SWE-bench ranges from 53.73 (Codex) to 60.47 (OpenHands). Both tables are single-source author runs; no independent replication or confidence intervals exist.

title: DeepSeek-V4-Pro Terminal-Bench 2.1: 87.9 / 72.1 self-reported vs 49.2 in NVIDIA's evaluation
description: DeepSeek reports 87.9 (V4-Pro-0813) and 72.1 (preview) on Terminal-Bench 2.1, while NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Ultra card lists 49.2 for DS-v4-Pro (and 74.5 vs DeepSeek's 80.6 on SWE-bench Verified). Checkpoint, harness and settings differ and are only partly stated; a neutral re-run is needed to reconcile them.

title: Kimi K2.6 SWE-bench Verified: 80.2 self-reported vs 75.7 in NVIDIA's evaluation
description: Moonshot's card reports 80.2 on SWE-bench Verified for Kimi K2.6; NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Ultra comparison table lists 75.7 for the same model. Neither run publishes trajectories in the card, so the 4.5-point gap cannot be attributed to harness, sampling or task fixes.

title: Headline agentic scores use each vendor's own (or a closed) harness, so cross-model tables are not like-for-like
description: Kimi K3 is scored with Kimi Code, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DeepSeek Harness, Qwen3.8-27B's SWE-bench Pro with the closed Claude Code harness, while competitor columns use "best reported harness". GLM-5.3's comparison table does not state the harness at all.

title: SWE-bench Pro results reported on a vendor-corrected task set
description: The Qwen3.8-27B card states that problematic SWE-bench Pro tasks were corrected and all baselines re-evaluated on the refined benchmark, and it also reports an in-house QwenSWEBench. Such numbers are not comparable with the official set unless the corrected task list is published.

title: Benchmark version/subset often missing from reported open-model claims
description: Claims cite "Terminal Bench 2" (Devstral Small 2), "DeepSWE" without version (GLM-5.2), "SWE-Bench (OpenHands)" without naming Verified (Nemotron 3 Super table), and HLE full vs text-only subsets interchangeably (DeepSeek marks text-only with a dagger). With TB 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 and DeepSWE v1/v1.1 coexisting, unversioned claims cannot be placed on the map reliably.

title: Terminal-Bench 3.0/4.0 results for open models exist only as vendor self-reports
description: Terminal-Bench v3.0.0 (Jul 2026) and v4.0.0 (Aug 2026) are released, but the only open-model numbers found are self-reported in the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GLM-5.3 cards; the tbench.ai leaderboard renders client-side and could not be checked mechanically. No open harness has a TB 3.0/4.0 result on an open model from a neutral party.

title: Terminal-Bench 2.1 leaderboard is closed to community submissions
description: The TB 2.1 README states community submissions are currently closed and only maintainer-run results are added, so community runs of open harnesses × open models have no official venue. A verified community result channel (like this project's T3 tier) is missing.

title: Aider polyglot leaderboard has no entries after 2025-10-03
description: The leaderboard data file's latest entries are dated 2025-10-03 (DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp) and the latest aider release is v0.86.0 (Aug 2025), so none of the 2026 open-weight models (DeepSeek V4.x, GLM-5.x, Kimi K3, Qwen3.8) appear.

title: Official SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench leaderboards are not mechanically quote-checkable
description: swebench.com and tbench.ai render scores client-side (fetched HTML text contains no result rows), and the SWE-bench leaderboards.json data file is ~4 MB, above a 3 MB fetch cap. Leaderboard-sourced claims therefore cannot reach T1 without a dedicated data-file adapter.

title: Key open-model results published only as images
description: Leanstral 1.5 (Lean 4 proof agent) and most of Mistral Medium 3.5's benchmark comparisons appear only as chart images on their model cards, so they cannot be quoted or source-checked; only two numbers (91.4% tau3-Telecom, 77.6% SWE-bench Verified) for Mistral Medium 3.5 are in text.

title: Flagship open-weight model cards report no standardized safety/jailbreak benchmark
description: The fetched cards for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3, Qwen3.8-27B and Nemotron 3 Ultra list dozens of capability benchmarks but no HarmBench/StrongREJECT-style jailbreak or refusal results, while GLM-5.3 highlights rising cyber-offense capability (CyberGym, ExploitGym).

title: Training data undisclosed for most frontier open-weight models
description: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 cards enumerate pre- and post-training datasets (including benchmark-adjacent sets such as SWE-Gym and SWE-bench_Verified listed in post-training data), but the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8-27B cards contain no dataset disclosure, so contamination of benchmarks like SWE-bench Verified cannot be assessed.

title: Popular open harnesses publish no benchmark results with open models
description: The READMEs of Goose, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw, Cline and OpenCode contain no benchmark scores; numbers for OpenCode exist only inside model vendors' cards. By contrast Qwen Code publishes a per-version SWE-bench Verified table, but only for a Qwen model.

title: No published evidence linking environment-hub environments to agentic benchmark gains
description: verifiers, OpenEnv and NeMo Gym READMEs describe environment APIs and hubs but report no results showing which environments improve SWE/terminal benchmarks; the closest public data point is Ai2's tmax-27b ("roughly 43%" on TB 2.0 after RL), which does not attribute gains to specific environments.

title: No new Meta Llama LLM weights since Llama 4 (April 2025)
description: The most recent meta-llama Hugging Face uploads are Llama 4 and Llama Guard 4 / Prompt Guard 2 (April 2025); Llama evidence on the map is therefore 18 months old and absent from all 2026 comparison tables fetched.

title: Self-reported vs leaderboard DeepSWE for Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3 diverge by harness
description: Kimi K3 reports 67.5 on DeepSWE with its own Kimi Code harness and 67.3 with mini-SWE-agent; the DeepSWE leaderboard page currently shows 69% for kimi-k3 [max] and 69% for glm-5.3 [max] (GLM self-reports 66.9). Which number the map should prefer, and under which version/date, is unresolved.
